grh_f8e897f04d941ce62a8d.title: The Other One
paragraphs: Edward lies to police to protect his troubled brother Randolph, who is suspected in the death of schoolgirl Miriam Winslow. Dr. Christian patiently works past Edwards fierce family loyalty and uncovers a pattern of theft, secret spending and desperate attempts by Randolph to impress Miriam. Edward finally admits that Randolph met the girl wearing a hidden new jacket, tried to force an expensive necklace on her, and killed her when the encounter turned violent. Dr. Christian helps Edward understand that protecting his brother with lies will only deepen the damage, and that telling the truth is the only way to help both Randolph and their family.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on February 21, 1951. It is listed as episode 638 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 32 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.5221eeeeadef88a8|Hair Tonic]] and [[org|org.eb32ba11a9b7bc34|and Lip Ice]].

grh_f86b84338de5f8450f2d.title: Tom Dick and Harry
paragraphs: Telephone operator Janie is courted by three very different men: practical Tom, wealthy and sophisticated Dick, and impulsive mechanic Harry. Unable to decide, she becomes engaged to all three and dreams through what marriage to each man might actually be like. Janie finally chooses Dick as the sensible answer, but his kiss leaves her unmoved; when Harry kisses her, the missing spark is obvious, and she runs off with the least practical man because he is the one she truly loves.

grh_f852ba0f950d8d7a3709.title: An Artist Comes To Town
paragraphs: When celebrated portrait painter Sylvia St. Vincent sweeps into Rivers End and demands the towns best doctor for an emergency, Dr. Christian discovers that the patient is her beloved dog rather than a person.
